evidence.clarity: H1 'Expected number. Got string.' is a hook (the error itself) rather than a description; the bolded line right under it, 'Contractcheck is a GitHub App for backend teams. On every pull request it runs your OpenAPI spec against your staging API, and fails the check when a response stops matching the spec', supplies what, who and the next action ('Install the GitHub App'). It is clear after the subhead, not the headline alone.
evidence.fit: Every ask has a deliberate resolution: the failing check is the hero artifact; staging-only is in the hero reassurance line, the nav ('Staging only') and a diagram with a 'Production API / Not part of any run / NEVER' node; the approver gets a calculator headed 'What the team lead approves'; the Postman replacement closes the timeline section. Tone is terse and engineering-native.
evidence.distinctiveness: The page takes its look from the product: the headline is a type-mismatch error, a condensed grotesk display face is paired with a monospace, and a rubber-stamp motif carries a real pass/fail meaning throughout (FAILED/PASSED on the run, 'FOUND HERE' vs 'FAILED' on the two timelines, FAILED on the setup strip, NEVER on production, FREE/$19 on pricing). Recognisable with the logo removed. The stamp on pricing is the one place it edges into decoration.
evidence.proof: 1440: an operable sample run sits beside the headline: 'Add currency back', 'Send total as a number', 'Document 409 in the spec' each flip a row to FIXED, the verdict recounts ('2 problems in 2 responses' and on to 'No problems. Both responses match openapi.yaml') and the stamp turns to PASSED. 'Edit this response body' re-checks live JSON. Counts stay consistent through every state I tried, and it is labelled 'SAMPLE' at the top and 'Example spec, requests and responses written for this page' at the foot.
evidence.craft: Deliberate scale (clamp-based h1/h2/lede tokens), consistent spacing tokens and a clear hierarchy; no defects at 1440, 768 or 390 in any state, and no text under 12px. Minor: at 1440 the problem rows use a narrow middle column, so JSON-pointer paths wrap to 3 lines ('#/paths/~1orders~1{id}~1cancel/post/responses'); the hero 'What fails the check' legend repeats what the sample already shows; the flat grey ground makes the lower sections feel a little dull.
evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed rather than shrunk. A 'Menu' button opens 44px-tall rows (Escape closes it; tapping 'Pricing' closes it and scrolls); the sample runs nearly edge to edge with the black 'SAMPLE' bar and the FAILED stamp in the first viewport; the fix buttons are 44px and the calculator input is 48px; the timelines are side by side and readable; no overflow at 320. Feedback appears in the tapped row ('409 is now documented... The check now passes.'), although the PASSED stamp is then off-screen above.
evidence.honesty: The sample is labelled where it appears, at the top in a black bar that is visible at 390 without scrolling. The config file is captioned 'Example of the shape. evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: each fix toggles to Undo and back, 'Reset the sample' restores '3 problems in 2 responses / FAILED', and changes are announced in a live region. In the body editor, broken JSON shows a 'Not JSON' row with the parse error, an empty body gives 'Empty body', an array gives 'Type changed... sent an array', and currency:5 gives 'currency: the spec says string. Staging sent 5.' The calculator handles '' ('Enter how many...'), -3, 2.5 and 1000 ('Enter a whole number from 0 to 999.') and 0 ('Public repositories only: nothing to pay.'). evidence.copy: Customer-world nouns and verbs throughout: 'Caught on the pull request, not in a client team's bug report', '"total is a string now?"', 'What the team lead approves', 'Make the next breaking response fail a check, not a client'. Button labels say what happens ('Send total as a number', 'Document 409 in the spec') and the microcopy is written ('Checked as you type.'). Small nits: the nav label 'Why the PR' is cryptic, and the pricing/staging reassurance line appears verbatim twice.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the hook, an explicit what/who line, 'Install the GitHub App', price plus staging-only, and a live failing sample with two problems visible all sit in one viewport. 390: the headline, lede, CTA, reassurance, SAMPLE label, FAILED stamp and '3 problems in 2 responses' are in view. The promise is carried by the subhead rather than the headline, so it lands one beat later than it could.

problems: The headline 'Expected number. Got string.' names the problem, not the outcome; what and who depend on the bolded subhead.
At 1440 the problem rows' narrow middle column makes JSON-pointer paths wrap to three lines, and the hero legend repeats what the sample already shows.
At 390 the PASSED stamp and verdict are off-screen when you fix the last problem at the bottom of the card (the row text does confirm it), and the nav label 'Why the PR' is unclear.

reason: B has a visual point of view drawn from the product (an error-message headline, condensed type, a stamp motif that carries pass/fail meaning) and a sample check the visitor can actually fix, edit and reset, labelled at the top even on a phone and recomposed properly for 390. A is clean and its spec-vs-response diff is very legible, but outside that card it is a stock dev-tool template, its artifact is a two-state toggle and its mobile targets are undersized. I would change my mind if the stamp motif tested as gimmicky with engineers, or if A's side-by-side diff proved meaningfully clearer than B's text rows.
